easy.q: Elder Schmeil said God gave us “divine helps” to return to Him. Which two did he talk about?
options: Good friends and good teachers
The Savior Jesus Christ and our covenants
Strong bodies and sharp minds
easy.why: Elder Schmeil said, “I will mention two of these divine helps: the Savior Jesus Christ and our covenants.” God did not leave us alone on our journey home.

easy.q: In the Old Testament story Elder Schmeil told, what had the Lord commanded the Israelites to do?
options: Rebuild the temple
Build a great ship
Plant a new vineyard
easy.why: The Lord had commanded the Israelites to rebuild the temple, but they were busy with their own houses and did not put His house first.

easy.q: What happened as soon as the Israelites started to rebuild the temple?
options: The Lord told them to stop and rest
The Lord sent them to a new land
The Lord promised to bless them from that day
easy.why: When they repented and began the work, the Lord said, “From this day will I bless you.” He is eager to bless us when we follow Him.

easy.q: Elder Schmeil taught that Jesus Christ gave us the sacrament to help us remember Him. What is promised if we do?
options: We will have His Spirit with us
We will never have a hard day
We will know every answer
easy.why: The Savior instituted the sacrament to help us remember Him, with the promise that if we do, we will have His Spirit with us.

easy.q: Which words of the Lord did Elder Schmeil ask us to apply to our own lives?
options: “Count your blessings”
“Lift up your eyes”
“Consider your ways”
easy.why: The Lord told the Israelites, “Consider your ways,” and Elder Schmeil said, “May we also consider our ways.” It means looking honestly at what we put first.

medium.q: Elder Schmeil said a central feature of humility is having a broken heart. What did he say a broken heart means?
options: To feel sorrow so deep that hope is gone
To be receptive to the will of God
To be let down by people we trusted
To give up on what we want the most
medium.why: He taught that a broken heart “means to be receptive to the will of God.” It is an open, teachable heart, not a hopeless one.

medium.q: The Savior said, “Take my yoke upon you.” According to Elder Schmeil, how do we become yoked with Him?
options: By carrying our burdens without complaint
By finishing our work before we rest
By staying away from those who trouble us
Through the covenants we make with God
medium.why: Elder Schmeil said, “It is through covenants that we become yoked with the Savior Jesus Christ and our burdens become lighter.”

medium.q: In Haggai, the Israelites earned wages only “to put it into a bag with holes.” Why, in Elder Schmeil's telling, were they doing much but accomplishing little?
options: They had too few workers for the harvest
Their enemies kept taking what they earned
God’s holy house was not a priority for them
They had planted in the wrong season
medium.why: Elder Schmeil explained that the Lord could not magnify their efforts because their actions were not aligned with His will; His holy house was not a priority in their lives.

medium.q: What did Elder Schmeil say the sacrament prayer reminds us about partaking of the sacrament?
options: We must have a week free of mistakes
We need to be willing, not perfect
We must feel no doubts of any kind
We need to have earned His Spirit
medium.why: He said we “do not need to be perfect to partake of the sacrament.” We need to be willing to take His name upon us, remember Him, and keep His commandments.

medium.q: Elder Schmeil quoted Elder Renlund about a time when we may hesitate to go to church. What was Elder Renlund’s counsel for that time?
options: Go and partake of the sacrament with a broken heart
Stay home until the hesitation has passed
Wait for a visit from a ward leader first
Study alone until every question is settled
medium.why: Elder Renlund promised that if we go and partake of the sacrament with a broken heart and a contrite spirit, blessings will keep us firm on the foundation that is Jesus Christ.

hard.q: Elder Schmeil linked humility and faith. According to him, what must we have in order to be receptive to the will of God?
options: A clear view of why each trial has come
A record of keeping every commandment
Faith in Christ, trusting Him without all the answers
An assurance that our burden will soon be lifted
hard.why: He taught that to be receptive to God’s will we must have faith in Christ, “which means that we trust Him even when we don’t have all the answers.”

hard.q: In the definition of a covenant that Elder Schmeil quoted, who sets the conditions of the covenant?
options: God and His children settle them together
God gives them, and His children agree to obey
Each person offers what he or she is able to give
Church leaders set them to fit each member
hard.why: The definition says, “God gives the conditions for the covenant, and His children agree to obey those conditions.” God then promises to bless them as they fulfill it.

hard.q: How did Elder Schmeil connect the sacrament to temple covenants?
options: The sacrament stands in for them when a temple is far away
Temple covenants make the weekly sacrament less needed
The two are separate and serve unrelated purposes
The sacrament prepares us to make and keep them
hard.why: He said, “The sacrament also prepares us to make and keep temple covenants,” and later testified that it has helped him keep his baptismal and temple covenants.

hard.q: Which situation best fits what Elder Schmeil drew from Haggai?
options: A man who feels he gets nowhere decides to work longer hours
A woman waits for a clear blessing before she changes anything
A busy family that feels little progress reorders its week to put God first
A student drops most of his duties so that he can finally rest
hard.why: The Israelites were “doing much” but “not accomplishing much” because their actions were not aligned with God’s will. The answer was to change priorities, not simply to do more or less.

hard.q: Applying Haggai to us, Elder Schmeil said Heavenly Father is not asking us to physically build the temple. What did he say God is asking us to build?
options: A strong relationship with Him and His Son through covenants
A habit of working harder and longer than before
A deeper knowledge of Old Testament history
A life with fewer duties and more time to rest
hard.why: He said God “is asking us to build a strong relationship with Him and His Son, Jesus Christ, through our covenants,” and will magnify our efforts as we make the proper adjustments.
